description: Learn how to build lesson slides faster from a lesson plan on your Mac. Save time, reduce burnout, and keep your teaching focused with these practical steps.

intro: You can build lesson slides faster from a lesson plan by shifting your focus from design to structure first. Teachers often lose hours each week manually formatting slides when they should be refining their pedagogy.
tldr: Stop designing individual slides first and start with a clear, text-based lesson outline.
Use your Mac to batch-create content before moving it into Keynote or Google Slides.
Leverage dictation to get your thoughts from your head into your planning documents instantly.
Keep your slide decks simple to serve as a visual guide rather than a script.

blocks.text: The hidden cost of manual slide creation

Building lesson slides is rarely just about adding images or picking a font. It is a production cycle that consumes your evenings. When you sit down to build a deck, you are often fighting with alignment, finding images, and trying to fit text into boxes. This is why 71% of teachers report doing this work outside of their paid hours. It is not just the slides. It is the supporting materials like handouts and quizzes that double the time investment.
Why you spend too much time on design

The primary cause of this bottleneck is the 'slide-first' mentality. Many teachers open Keynote or Google Slides before they have a finished plan. You end up making design choices while you should be making pedagogical ones. This leads to constant re-editing. You change a slide, then realize the flow is wrong, then change it again. The structural burden of organizing content is what really drains your time, accounting for 58% of the difficulty.
Fixes to build lesson slides faster

items: Write your lesson plan as a simple bulleted list in Pages or Google Docs first.
Use the ⌘ ⇧ D shortcut to trigger system-wide dictation, getting your plan written while you talk through the lesson flow.
Keep your slide design minimal. Use a consistent theme so you do not have to think about layouts for every new slide.
Group your slides by lesson section rather than trying to build a linear deck from start to finish.
Reuse your best templates. If you have a slide layout that works for a 'Do Now' activity, save it as a master slide.

blocks.text: How Lazur helps you save time

Lazur acts as a bridge between your plan and your slides. Instead of manually typing every bullet point into a presentation app, you can use Lazur to dictate the content directly into your document or slide notes. If you get stuck on a layout, hold ⌥ ⌘ to ask where a specific tool is, and Lazur will point it out on your screen.
A daily routine for efficient planning

items: Morning: Review your learning goals. Use dictation to capture the core concepts for the day.
Afternoon: Structure the lesson in a text document. Do not touch your presentation app yet.
Evening: Open your slide template. Copy your text into the slides. Keep designs simple.

faq.question: Does Lazur build the slides for me?
faq.answer: No. Lazur does not click buttons or create files for you. It helps you work faster by pointing out tools, answering questions, and dictating text.

faq.question: Can I use Lazur to write my lesson plans?
faq.answer: Yes. You can use the dictation feature to speak your lesson plan into any app, which is much faster than typing.
